setup.zh: 河伯没走。他悬在漳水正中，踩着两条龙，低头看着你的胸口：「……你身上，有青丘的味道。」河心底下，有一样东西在一明一暗地呼吸。
setup.en: The River Lord has not gone. He hangs over the middle of the Zhang on his two dragons, looking down at your chest: "…You smell of Qingqiu." Deep in mid-river, something breathes, light and dark, light and dark.

recap.zh: 二十五个姑娘活在柳湾；拦船的老胡死在城楼底下——把河伯请上来的，是你。河伯原是冰夷；他守了两千年的东西在河心坑底，上头压着洛书之封。你潜下去，呛了水，差一点没上来；数错了一回，又改了过来。
recap.en: The twenty-five girls were alive at Willow Bend; Old Hu, who came to stop the boat, died under the tower — and it was you who brought the River Lord up. The River Lord was Bingyi; what he had kept two thousand years lay in the pit mid-river under the Luo seal. You dived, choked, nearly did not come up; you counted wrong once, and set it right.

zh: 二十五个姑娘，一个也没死。
en: Twenty-five girls, and not one dead.
A light at the bottom of the pit: light, dark.

story.zh:
二十五个姑娘，一个也没死。来拦船的那一个爹，死在了城楼底下。

河伯没走。他悬在漳水正中，踩着两条龙，低头看着小满——说得准些，是看着他胸口。他开口的时候，嘴唇却没有动，那声音是从小满脚底下的水里漫上来的，一个字一个字，只往他一个人耳朵里钻：「……你身上，有青丘的味道。」

小满张着嘴，一个字也说不出来。银月钻了出来，蹲在他肩膀上，这一回，岸上的人都看不见她，只有他和河伯看得见。她瞧着河伯，开口便道：「……冰夷。」

这两个字一出口，她自己倒先愣了一愣，仿佛这名字不是想起来的，是从嘴里自己掉出来的。河伯看着她，眼神晃了一下。他道：「……你。你还活着。」他的眼睛落到她身后那一条尾巴上，便不说话了。银月也没有说话，把那条尾巴往身子底下收了一收。

小满压着嗓子问道：「冰夷？」银月道：「他的本名。『河伯』，是你们凡人叫的。」

河伯没理银月，又看了小满一眼，道：「那婆子掉下来的时候，在我水里喊。她喊的不是河伯。她喊『仙长』。」又道：「……那仙长是谁？」

小满往河里走了两步，站在齐膝深的水里，压低了声音——站在他的水里，说什么他都听得见——把那两锭大银、庙里那个脚下没声的白衣人，还有那白衣人的两句话，一样一样说了。说到「去年漳水涨了三尺，今年，他该忍不住了」，河伯的脸色变了。说到「他上来的时候，你们谁也不许拦」，河伯半晌没有作声。

过了很久，他才道：「……原来如此。」那声音里没有怒气，只有一股说不出的疲倦，「我在这水底下两千年，没挪过窝。我从哪里上来，底下便压着什么。漳水长八百里，他们找不着；便一年砸一个姑娘下来，砸我，砸了二十五年，等我自己浮上来。」他望着东边的城墙，「修士动我，天上要往下看；凡人往河里扔媳妇，天上不看。……好算计。」

小满听到这里，手脚一阵冰凉。那个圈，那锭银子，那个白衣人——他们花了二十五年、两千五百两银子，没能做成的事，他一个上午便替他们做成了。他把巫祝扔下了河，他把河伯请了上来。

把河伯请上来的，是他。拍塌那一角城楼的，是他请上来的那一巴掌。

银月蹲在他肩上，一个字也没有说。

河伯道：「两千年前，有人托我守它。她说，会有人来拿。拿的人，身上有青丘的味道。」又道：「光有味道不够。方才那两条龙，是替她问你的。」

等岸上的人散尽，日头已挨着了西边的城墙，小满才下了水。
story.en:
Twenty-five girls, and not one of them dead. The one father who came to stop the boat lay dead under the tower.

The River Lord did not go. He hung over the middle of the Zhang on his two dragons, looking down at Xiaoman — at his chest, to be exact. When he spoke his lips did not move; the voice welled up from the water under Xiaoman's feet, word by word, into his ears alone: "…You smell of Qingqiu."

Xiaoman stood with his mouth open and not a word came. Yinyue slipped out and sat on his shoulder; this time no one on the bank could see her, only he and the River Lord. She looked at the River Lord and said straight out: "…Bingyi."

The moment the name was out, she seemed startled herself, as if the name had not been remembered but had fallen out of her mouth on its own. The River Lord looked at her, and his gaze wavered. He said: "…You. You're alive." His eyes went to the single tail behind her, and he said no more. Yinyue said nothing either, and tucked that tail in under herself.

Xiaoman asked under his breath: "Bingyi?" Yinyue said: "His own name. 'River Lord' is what you mortals call him."

The River Lord paid Yinyue no heed and looked at Xiaoman again: "When the old woman fell in, she cried out in my water. Not for the River Lord. She cried 'Immortal Master'." Then: "…Who is this Immortal Master?"

Xiaoman waded two steps into the river and stood knee-deep, and lowered his voice — standing in his water, whatever he said would be heard — and told it all, one thing after another: the two big ingots, the man in white at the temple who made no sound when he walked, and that man's two sentences. At "Last year the Zhang rose three feet; this year he won't be able to hold himself back," the River Lord's face changed. At "When he comes up, none of you is to stop him," the River Lord said nothing for a long while.

After a long while he said: "…So that is how it is." There was no anger in his voice, only a weariness past words. "Two thousand years I have lain under this water and never moved. Where I come up, there is what I sit on. The Zhang runs eight hundred li; they could not find it — so they dropped a girl on me once a year, struck me, twenty-five years, waiting for me to surface myself." He looked toward the eastern wall. "If cultivators touch me, Heaven looks down; if mortals throw brides into a river, Heaven does not look. …A neat sum."

At this Xiaoman went cold to his hands and feet. The circle, the ingot, the man in white — what they had spent twenty-five years and two thousand five hundred taels and failed to do, he had done for them in one morning. He had thrown the shaman into the river; he had brought the River Lord up.

It was he who had brought the River Lord up. The blow that brought down that corner of the tower was the one he had called up.

Yinyue sat on his shoulder and did not say a word.

The River Lord said: "Two thousand years ago someone asked me to guard it. She said someone would come for it. The one who came would smell of Qingqiu." Then he said: "The smell alone is not enough. Those two dragons just now — they were asking you on her behalf."

Only when the bank had emptied and the sun was touching the western wall did Xiaoman go into the water.

label.en: Read the seal · Fill the heart

exits.means: reads the seal, answers what belongs in the middle square

story.zh:
他一慌，张嘴便呛进了一口冰水。那水像一把刀，顺着喉咙割进胸口里。他拼命地咳，越咳，灌进来的水越多。眼前那一点鼎光散了，散成一片一片的金星；手脚一下子轻了，轻得像不是他的。他心里很清楚地想：原来淹死是这样的。不疼，只是冷，冷了，就轻了。他又想起城楼底下那一只沾着豆渣的手。

便在这时，胸口的木牌，微微一热。只一点点，像冬夜里揣在怀里的一颗炭星。没有声音，只那么热了一下，便又凉了。

那一点热，把他的心定住了。他这才听见了自己的心：四下里什么都隔着一层，只有它隔不住，在胸口底下一下一下地撞，又急又乱。他不去管它，只听着；听着听着，那一下一下的撞，缓了，沉了。

他闭上眼睛。瞿老那十六个字，这时才知道分量：前八个字，那颗心方才已经替他做了；后八个字，说的便是方才那些「原来淹死是这样的」。他把那些乱想一个一个按下去，只往里看。水底下本来就黑，闭上眼睛，倒亮了。他看见了灶间那盏油灯，灯芯一跳一跳；看见他娘坐在灶台那一头，他坐在这一头；看见她把手指头伸进水碗里蘸了一蘸，在灶台上画格子，一边画，一边念：「戴九履一，左三右七，二四为肩，六八为足，五居中央。」她画完了，拿手指头点着，一格一格地教他：「三的底下，是八；七的底下，是六。记住了？」他说：「记住了。」她说：「记住了，就一辈子别忘。」

三的底下，是八。他伸手去摸左边那一只「足」上的石头，一个点一个点地数：一，二，三，四，五，六。六。他放反了。

他把左边那块六个点的拿起来，和右边那块八个点的，对调了过来。左八，右六。

然后他把那块五个点的石头，最后一块——第九块——按进了正中那一格。

这一回，它进去了。只听得「咔」的一声轻响，那声音不大，他在水底下却听得清清楚楚，便如沈家那扇装歪了的门，终于给人扶正了，落进了门臼里。
story.en:
He panicked, opened his mouth, and choked on ice water. It went down his throat like a knife, into his chest. He coughed and coughed, and the more he coughed the more water came in. The light of the cauldron scattered into sparks of gold; his hands and feet went suddenly light, as if they were not his. Very clearly he thought: so this is drowning. It doesn't hurt; it is only cold, and then light. And he thought of the hand under the tower with soybean pulp on it.

Just then the token at his chest grew faintly warm. Only a little, like an ember carried inside your coat on a winter night. No voice — just that one warmth, and then it was cool again.

That little warmth steadied his heart. Only then did he hear it: everything around him was muffled, all but this, thudding under his breastbone beat after beat, fast and wild. He did not try to master it; he only listened; and as he listened the beats slowed and grew heavy.

He shut his eyes. Only now did he feel the weight of Old Qu's sixteen characters: the first eight his heart had just done for him; the last eight were about all that "so this is what drowning is". He pressed those wild thoughts down one by one and looked only inward. It was dark under the water to begin with; with his eyes shut, it grew bright. He saw the oil lamp in the kitchen, its wick jumping; his mother at one end of the stove and himself at the other; saw her dip a finger in the water bowl and draw a grid on the stovetop, chanting as she drew: "Nine on the head, one at the feet, three on the left, seven on the right, two and four the shoulders, six and eight the feet, five in the middle." When she had drawn it she pointed square by square and taught him: "Under three is eight; under seven is six. Got it?" He said: "Got it." She said: "Then never forget it as long as you live."

Under three, eight. He reached for the stone on the left foot and counted it dot by dot: one, two, three, four, five, six. Six. He had them the wrong way round.

He took up the six-dot stone on the left and swapped it with the eight-dot stone on the right. Eight left, six right.

Then he took the five-dot stone, the last one — the ninth stone — and pressed it into the middle square.

This time it went in. There was a soft click — not loud, but under the water he heard it clearly — like the Shen family's crooked door finally set straight and dropped into its socket.

exits.means: tries to break, lift or pry the slab by force

text.zh: 石板纹丝不动。九个数在你掌下微微发烫。
text.en: The slab does not move. The nine numbers grow warm under your palm.
